messages.text: Is it true Min-jun lost his money on that stock?
Most of it. He put everything into one company
When I retired, I spread my savings over many companies and some bonds
One of them went bankrupt last year. Your dad barely noticed 😄

steps.title: Not all eggs in one basket
steps.body: Spreading money over many investments is called [[diversification]]. If one company fails, it is only a small part of what you own. Putting a big share into one place is [[concentration-risk]].

steps.prompt: Dad spread his money equally over 20 companies. One goes bankrupt and is worth nothing. How much of his money does he lose?
steps.reveal: Each company was 1/20 of his money, so one bankruptcy costs 5%. Min-jun had 100% in one company: the same event took everything.

steps.prompt: One company crashes 60%. Change how much of your money is in it. Keep the damage to 10% or less.

goal.hint: Bring the share in one company down to about one sixth.

steps.note: Illustration only. The rest of the money is assumed flat.

steps.prompt: Match each idea from the Seoul story with its meaning.
pairs: A big share of your money in one place
Hype a price up, sell, let it crash
